intended_object: The standard identification Ext^n(X, Y) ≅ H^n(Hom^•(P_•, Y)) for a projective resolution P_• → X in an abelian category: Ext classes correspond to cohomology classes of degree n of morphisms of complexes from the resolution to Y placed in degree 0. Inferred from the docstring and the module doc ("Computing Ext using a projective resolution").
explanation:
The definition has the right type, `Ext X Y n ≃ CohomologyClass R.cochainComplex ((singleFunctor C 0).obj Y) n`, which is exactly H^n(Hom(P, Y[0])). It is built in two steps, and both are canonical:

1. Precompose with the quasi-isomorphism `R.π'` from the resolution to X placed in degree 0. This identifies shifted homs out of X[0] with shifted homs out of P in the localized (derived) category.
2. Use `equivOfIsKProjective`. Since P is a bounded-above complex of projectives (the instance declared just above), it is K-projective, so morphisms out of it in the derived category are the same as cohomology classes of the Hom complex.

This is the textbook isomorphism. The rest of the library uses it as such: it is shown to be additive and linear, and it underlies `extMk`, `extMk_eq_zero_iff` and `extMk_surjective`.

The setting is any abelian category C with `HasExt`, which is the natural generality for Ext computed by projective resolutions, so the definition is not too narrow. A cohomology class of degree n from a complex concentrated in nonpositive degrees to Y[0] matches the usual cohomology of Hom(P_•, Y). There are no degenerate-case problems: n is a natural number and the resolution is arbitrary.

I found no other Mathlib declaration giving this same equivalence.
